A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study, with matching authors, core experiments and contributions. Their text, figures, tables, equations and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original human psychophysics, evaluations of over 1,000 models, model-training interventions and supplementary experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and reports additional analyses of human performance, receptive-field alignment, background color and architecture differences.

M1.justification: The stimulus-generation approach, zero-shot mapping, linear decoders, ResNet-18 architecture and joint training objective remain unchanged. Appendix A.11 documents the existing stimulus generator more explicitly; it does not establish a changed procedure.

E1.justification: v2 adds evaluations against macaque V1 grating-summation-field and surround-diameter alignment benchmarks, plus a red-background test scenario (A.5 and A.13). The original object-recognition tasks, training datasets and human population are retained.

E2.justification: The model families, GPT-4o and Stylized ImageNet-trained ResNet-50 comparator are retained. Contour-training variants omitted from the simplified main Figure 7 remain in Appendix A.6/Figure 12, which reproduces v1's full comparison.

E3.justification: New protocols include restricting CNN–ViT comparisons to ImageNet-1k-trained models and testing 21 models with black versus red backgrounds. Figure 8 also shows a substantially enlarged plotted sample, but its membership is unspecified and Appendix A.10 still describes 50 models. Existing main training and human-testing settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands supplementary investigation through human slope comparisons, receptive-field alignment correlations, background-color robustness and architecture comparisons controlling training-dataset identity (A.4, A.5, A.13 and A.14). The ImageNet correlation analysis is revised. The contour-training controls in A.6 are relocated evidence, not new ablations.

E5.justification: Appendix A.4 adds a formal comparison of human performance slopes, and A.14 explicitly specifies a 0.01 significance criterion for architecture comparisons. Existing 95% confidence-interval reporting is retained; neither version documents additional repeated runs or random seeds.

E6.justification: Substantial supplementary results are added, including receptive-field correlations of 0.2655 and 0.276 and the background comparison t = 0.323, p = 0.749. Figure 8 replaces r = 0.728 with r = 0.67 alongside a changed plotted sample, not a demonstrated same-setting performance decline. Main tables remain unchanged. A.14 reports CNN/ViT accuracies of 32.49%/31.24%, whereas Figure 15's average-performance bars are near 11%, without explaining the discrepancy.

T1.justification: Appendix A.11 adds explicit mathematical definitions of the orientation-selective filter and quadrature-based contour map in Equations 2–3. This expands the formal specification of the existing generator; the training objective is unchanged and no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract and five introductory contributions are unchanged. The central claims about human–model differences, dataset scaling, integration bias and induced shape bias are retained; the new analyses primarily supply supporting evidence.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations concerning largely parallel human scaling curves, weak receptive-field associations, background robustness and similar architecture performance. It also explicitly interprets retained contour controls as excluding an image-statistics explanation and proposes smaller trained models for mechanistic investigation. Existing limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix A.11 newly discloses FFT-based convolution, filter parameters sigma = 0.06 arcdeg and lambda = 0.12 arcdeg, and contour-dependent element placement. These improve documentation of existing synthesis. Training recipes, hardware information and GPT-4o settings are retained.

R1.justification: v2 acknowledges earlier non-DNN contour modeling through Li (1998) and adds Cavanaugh et al. (2002) and Marques et al. (2021) for the receptive-field benchmarks. The broader positioning and novelty claims remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Most main-text prose is retained. Changes include moving the detailed contour-training comparison into the appendix, adding explanatory passages and appendix subsections, and updating acknowledgements and publication information. There is no extensive narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: v2 materially expands visual evidence with human scaling, receptive-field, background-control and CNN–ViT plots. Figure 7 is simplified and relabeled while its original full version becomes Figure 12; Figure 8 is redrawn with a different scatter and axis scale. Tables 1–3 retain their structure and contents.

improvement.justification: The explicit synthesis parameters improve reproducibility, and targeted supplementary controls examine alternative explanations absent from v1. These are limited gains: Figure 8's enlarged sample is not reconciled with the retained 50-model description, and A.14's numerical results are not reconciled with Figure 15. The principal evidence and conclusions remain intact.
